To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mechanical properties of nanocrystallines bcc iron were investigated by MD simulations, and a breakdown in the hall-petch relation was observed for grain sizes below 13.5 nm.

(1) average flow stress of NC Fe decreases with decreasing grain size, (2) the Hall-Petch breakdown may be due to a change from GB mediated dislocation activities (for large grain size) to GB activities (for small grain size), (3) the flow stress increases with decreasing temperature and increasing strain rate, and (4) significant phase transformations occurred in the GB zone due to GB activities, while significant phase transformations occurred at stacking fault zone due the dislocation activities.

the mechanical properties of NC Fe and the effects of grain refinement, temperature and strain rate.

the mechanical properties of bcc Fe with grain size ranging from 13.54 to 1.71 nm under tensile deformation at temperatures from 300 K to 1200 K, with strain rates ranging from 10(7) s(-1) to 10(9) s(-1).

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the tensile deformation behavior of NC bcc Fe depends on the competition between dislocation activities and GB activities, and the deformation behavior is strongly dependent on the deformation temperature and the strain rate.
the Hall-Petch breakdown in bulk NC bcc Fe is due to GB activities and stress induced phase transformations.
the tensile strength of NC bcc Fe increases with decreasing grain size and increasing strain rates and deformation temperatures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mechanical properties of NC Fe depend not only on the grain sizes but also on the deformation temperature and strain rates.
the mechanical properties of NC bcc Fe are strongly dependent on the grain size, temperature, and strain rate.
GB activities play a more important role than dislocation activities in the mechanical behaviors of bulk NC Fe under tensile loading.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mechanical properties of NC bcc Fe are strongly dependent on temperature, strain rates and grain size.
MD simulations can be a useful tool to study mechanical properties and stress induced phase transformations of bulk NC metals.
the deformation mechanisms of bulk NC Fe are strongly dependent on the grain size, strain rate, and deformation temperature.
